thread:
incident-bot: [P1] alert at 2026-10-12T19:14:38Z - spike of model load failures in pool inference-south-a. Samples show OOM/CUDA errors and deserialization exceptions during warmup. Impacting capacity; auto-retry causing container restarts.

Alex G: ack'ing, I'm oncall. @here please triage. Links: runbook -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-load-failures. Paging phone now.

Maria V: I'm looking. Noting a cluster of failures after the 02:00 deploy of runtime-lib 1.8.4. Logs: 
```
runtime: loading model gpt-small-1-8k-quant
error: DeserializationError: missing shards for tensor 'lm_head.weight' expected 8 got 4
trace: RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory at /src/runtime/cuda/allocator.cpp:234
container: process exited with signal 6 (SIGABRT)
```

Cheng L: seeing the same. The model bundle manifest references new sharded format (shard_count=8) but some nodes only pulled 4 shards before crash. Likely partial artifact replication + aggressive warmup causing OOM during deserialization.

Jamie K: Support note: ~15 customers showing 5xxs over last 10m, top hits: AcmeCorp (15% of requests), ProDocs (12%). No high-dollar legal customers yet but could escalate. Should we post a status? :warning:

Alex G: yes, prepare status page with "degraded performance" and note we are mitigating. @Derek S, can we route traffic off this pool?

Derek S: we can route. Recommend switching new requests to gpt-small-1-4k-quant (smaller mem profile) and enabling immutable fallback to that model for the pool while we investigate. Maria, can you apply?

Maria V: applying routing change now. Running admin command: 
```
# switch all traffic in pool to smaller variant
rictl route set --pool inference-south-a --model gpt-small-1-4k-quant --weight 100 --reason "mitigate warmup OOMs"
```

incident-bot: route change queued -> applied in 8s. Observability: new request success rate +30% within 45s.

Cheng L: mitigation helped immediate traffic. But warmup jobs still failing on nodes that already pulled the broken bundle and are stuck in restart loop. We should drain those nodes to stop churn. Node list: gpu-south-a-12,gpu-south-a-18,gpu-south-a-19.

Alex G: ok @Maria please cordon + drain those nodes. Use graceful pod eviction to let model servers fail warmup and not restart.

Maria V: cordoning/draining now: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-south-a-12 && kubectl drain gpu-south-a-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=5m
kubectl cordon gpu-south-a-18 && kubectl drain gpu-south-a-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=5m
kubectl cordon gpu-south-a-19 && kubectl drain gpu-south-a-19 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=5m
```

Maria V: drain in progress. Also bumped TVM compile timeout for warmup from 60s -> 180s as a short-term to avoid spurious compile timeouts during deserialization stalls: 
```
# config update
sed -i 's/compile_timeout_ms: 60000/compile_timeout_ms: 180000/' /etc/redwood/runtime-config.yaml && rictl config reload
```

Cheng L: long-term note: artifact replication service had a race condition where a node could mark bundle as "available" before all shards finished transfer. I'll open a fix and a retrospective. For immediate fix, I'll force re-sync of bundles and mark the bad partial artifact as invalid.

Jamie K: drafting status now. Proposed copy: "We are experiencing intermittent 5xx errors for model generation in the S. America region. Traffic is being rerouted to a lower-memory variant and engineering is investigating root cause. No customer data exposure. More updates in 30m." Need approval. :writing_hand:

Derek S: LGTM — send. Also notify enterprise customers (AcmeCorp) directly via provided SLA channel.

incident-bot: notification sent to customers subscribed to impacted pool.

Alex G: root-cause hypothesis for triage note: new runtime-lib (1.8.4) + partial artifact replication -> deserialization attempts on partial checkpoint -> repeated OOMs during warmup -> container crash loop -> capacity drop.

Cheng L: corroborating - deserializer should detect missing shards earlier and fail fast without allocating large GPU buffers. I'll add a guard to do shard count verification before GPU allocations. Low-risk patch, will push to canary later today.

Maria V: current metrics: CPU ok, GPU mem free on healthy nodes, success rate for pool improved to 95% after routing change and drains. Crash loop count decreased from 120/h -> 3/h.

Jamie K: status page updated and customer DM templates sent to a subset. Monitoring alert annotated with mitigation actions.

Alex G: handing off to next oncall @Taylor M for the 20:00–04:00 UTC window. Summary for handoff: P1 warmup load failures in inference-south-a caused by partial artifact replication + runtime-lib mismatch; mitigation applied: traffic rerouted to smaller variant, problematic nodes drained, TVM compile timeout increased, artifact re-sync in progress. Current status: degraded -> recovering. Watchlist: crash loop count, artifact re-sync success, customer 5xx count.

Taylor M: taking over. I'll keep an eye and confirm artifact re-sync finishes + validate patch rollouts. If crash loops reappear, I'll revert runtime-lib 1.8.4 across the pool.

Alex G: thanks team, leaving notes in incident tracker. Assigning follow-ups: Cheng to push deserializer guard (issue #INC-4021), Maria to create a canary for runtime-lib rollback (INC-4022), Derek to coordinate customer comms for enterprise accounts (INC-4023).

Cheng L: created INC-4021 with PR link: https://git.redwood/infer/deserializer/pull/89. Maria created INC-4022.

Taylor M: acknowledged handoff. I'll update the thread if anything changes. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident P1 -> status updated to "monitoring" at 2026-10-12T19:23:60Z.
